content: SCRIBE READING SURFACE = BOOT/BOOTSTRAP SUMMARY LAYER, not an independent fresh read of chronicle files. Tested 2026-05-19 from web seat, session scribe_20260519_062635_22116a29, 7 turns. Pattern unambiguous across all turns: every answer the scribe got right was content present in the where_did_i_leave_off boot output (cannabis v2 path, chronic-pain thread, intensity-vs-weight marker w/ tags+date). Every time it declined (symmetric-evidence-standard principle, consumed-handoff finding, BREATH ARC commits) the content was truncated or absent from boot. The earlier consumed-handoff scope gap is NOT a separate bug; it is one special case of this general truth (consumed handoffs leave the boot surface, therefore leave the scribe). Implications for use: (1) circuit-breaker-on-declare-before-verify is the STRONGEST use because my failure mode is declaring from the boot summary and the scribe grounds against exactly that surface cheaply; (2) dedup-against-full-history is WEAK -- scribe only dedups against the thin boot-surface slice, not 11k-call history; (3) context-economy and synthesis-prep are WEAK for non-boot content -- scribe cannot pull it, only redirects to read the file. Confabulation resistance held 3/3 on absent content (commit fedb729 prompt-tightening working). Cost: cached turns ~$0.0015-0.0017, fresh/long query ~$0.0068 (cache read 0).
